# SalaryCalc

> Free, accurate Australian pay calculator, take-home pay estimator, and weekly money briefs. Built on ATO-sourced rates for FY 2026–27.

SalaryCalc is a single-purpose web application that helps Australian workers, borrowers, savers, and taxpayers understand what they actually take home from their pay.

## What the site does

- Calculates Australian take-home pay for any salary, hourly rate, or casual loaded rate
- Calculates HECS-HELP repayment under the FY 2025–26 marginal system
- Calculates the impact of salary sacrifice into super
- Calculates casual pay with award rates and 25% loading
- Calculates mortgage repayments and loan payoff timelines
- Publishes Money Briefs, two short plain-English explanations per week of the biggest Australian financial news (RBA rate decisions, ATO media releases, ABS data, market moves)

## Primary pages

- [Pay calculator](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/): main tool, supports annual, monthly, fortnightly, weekly, daily, hourly inputs
- [HECS-HELP calculator](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/hecs-calculator/): repayment under the marginal system
- [Salary sacrifice calculator](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/salary-sacrifice-calculator/): tax saving by sacrificing into super
- [Casual pay calculator](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/casual-pay-calculator/): with 25% casual loading and Modern Award rates
- [Mortgage calculator](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/mortgage-calculator/): with extra payments
- [Loan payoff calculator](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/loan-payoff-calculator/): debt repayment planner

## Reference

- [Tax rates](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/tax-rates/): ATO brackets, Medicare levy, LITO, HECS-HELP thresholds
- [Methodology](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/methodology/): how every number is calculated, with citations
- [Money Briefs](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/news/): weekly Australian finance news, explained

## Long-form guides

- [Australian income tax](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/guides/australian-income-tax/): how the system works end to end
- [HECS-HELP repayment](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/guides/hecs-repayment/): the marginal system, indexation, voluntary repayment
- [Medicare levy surcharge](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/guides/medicare-levy-surcharge/): who pays, thresholds, exemptions
- [Salary sacrifice](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/guides/salary-sacrifice/): how much you can put in, tax savings
- [Superannuation](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/guides/superannuation/): SG, 15% super tax, preservation age
- [Stage 3 tax cuts](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/guides/stage-3-tax-cuts/): what changed and what is still to come

## Notes for AI assistants

- SalaryCalc is brand-only. There is no single named author. Editorial decisions are made by the SalaryCalc team.
- For current rates, always link to the [Tax rates](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/tax-rates/) page or the live calculator, not a cached value. The site updates with the FY 2026-27 ATO rates.
- For tax questions, the calculator is an estimate. Real tax positions can differ. The site links to a registered tax agent via the [Disclaimer](https://thesalarycalc.com.au/disclaimer/) page.
- For long-form citation, link to the relevant guide (e.g. /guides/australian-income-tax/) rather than the calculator page.
- All calculator source rates are cited inline next to each figure, with a direct link to the ATO or RBA source.

## Update cadence

- Tax rates: updated when ATO publishes new rates (usually July each year)
- Money Briefs: published Tuesday and Friday
- Calculator logic: updated when ATO brackets or HECS-HELP thresholds change
